resources.string:
BentoBar draws the items you add (network speed, timer, calendar, tools…) on top of the status bar. Android only allows that through an accessibility service.

What BentoBar does with it: it reads the layout of the status bar, and nothing else, to find free space; it copies the colour of the status bar clock so your items match; and it runs system actions such as screenshot or lock when you pick them in its Tools menu.

It does not read other apps' windows, does not watch your keyboard, mouse or touches, and has no internet access.

Add, hide and organise items in your Googlebook\'s status bar.

BentoBar has no internet permission. Your settings, calendar events and everything it measures stay on this device. Its accessibility service reads only the status bar (its layout, and the colour of its clock), never other apps.
